A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Neuroverse3D. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and corresponding methods, equations, figures and tables can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original neuroimaging experiments, including segmentation and generation results, context-size studies, loss ablations and resource measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds domain-discrimination results, fusion-stage ablations including PET, and context-modality experiments.

M1.justification: The two-branch 3D U-Net, APSP processing, gradient rescaling, U-shaped fusion and losses remain unchanged. Figure 3 clarifies the convolution label as 1×1×1; the additional fusion configurations are experimental ablations rather than changes to the proposed model.

E1.justification: v2 extends evaluation to unseen PET segmentation and mismatched context modalities, using T1 targets with T2 or CT contexts. It also adds an auxiliary training-versus-held-out discrimination task. The original dataset coverage is retained; the PET data source is unspecified.

E2.justification: Figure 6 adds a few-shot task-specific comparator to the context-size comparison. The main comparison methods remain unchanged; Painter's added Figure 4 legend entry identifies an existing comparator. The newly mentioned nnUNet has no reported comparative result.

E3.justification: New protocols vary fusion from the deepest stage alone to all five stages, compare T1/T2/CT contexts with fixed T1 targets, and evaluate domain discrimination using accuracy, precision, recall and F1. Existing splits, preprocessing, training budgets and Dice/PSNR evaluation remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained loss and context-size studies, v2 adds direct fusion-stage ablations including unseen PET (Table 8), context-modality robustness tests (Table 9), and a domain-discrimination probe (Appendix B.1). These substantially expand examination of architectural choices and generalization conditions.

E5.justification: Both versions specify ten evaluations with different context sets and reporting of means and standard deviations in Appendix C.2. v2 clarifies random context selection without changing the stated repetition count or statistical procedure. Changed error-bar magnitudes are result changes.

E6.justification: v2 adds discriminator accuracy of 0.934, PET Dice ranging from 0.2870 to 0.5314 across fusion configurations, and T1-target 2D-to-3D PSNR of 26.63/14.15/12.27 with T1/T2/CT contexts. Figure 6 adds few-shot results, and Figure 4 enlarges Painter error bars. Tables 1 and 4–7 retain their values.

T1.justification: Equations 1–10 and the gradient-expectation proof in Appendix A.1 are retained. Terminology and index clarifications do not change the mathematical definitions, assumptions or derivation.

C1.justification: The introduction narrows the novelty statement from the first 3D ICL universal model for medical imaging to the first for neuroimaging. Claims concerning unlimited contexts, optimized losses and performance relative to other models remain substantively unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 identifies modality alignment as an applicability condition and interprets task-dependent degradation through context dependence. It also discusses denser fusion benefiting PET, domain discrimination as proxy evidence of shift, and context-size gains plateauing around 16 while prediction variability decreases.

D1.justification: v2 updates the advertised repository path from Neu3D to Neuroverse3D and explicitly labels 3D fusion kernels. Figures 12–13 remove disclosures specifying context size four and, for Figure 13, four few-shot training samples. Existing hardware and training details are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds explicit references to Brown et al.'s Language Models are Few-Shot Learners and Gong et al.'s 3DSAM-adapter, resolving earlier missing citations and supporting the 3D motivation. Novelty positioning is narrowed to neuroimaging; the broader related-work organization remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 retitles the paper, revises author information, edits the abstract and explanatory prose, consolidates four contribution bullets into three, and adds acknowledgements. The main section sequence and most exposition remain intact, with additional appendix subsections.

P2.justification: Retypesetting changes typography, spacing and figure placement throughout. Diagrams gain annotations, Figure 4 repairs its legend, Figure 6 gains a comparator series, and Tables 8–9 are added. Figure 5 expands from four to six tasks using examples already present in v1's appendix, rather than introducing new coverage.

improvement.justification: The fusion-stage and context-modality experiments strengthen architectural justification and reveal useful applicability limits; the added few-shot curve improves comparison. These gains are limited by sparse descriptions of the new PET and discriminator experiments and removal of context/sample-size information from qualitative captions. The evidence supports a modest overall improvement.
